title: +72% In Five Months: Records In A War Zone, And Still A BUY
description: Records on every line, a first-ever dividend, and a target raised from $41.50 to $47. The stock stays a BUY.
body_html:
Since adding my March pick to the portfolio, it is up 72% in five months.

Back on March 16, I sent a trade alert buying this company’s stock while missiles were flying over.

Four days later, I published the full deep dive.

The pushback in my inbox was immediate: who buys into an active war?

Since I moved to North America more than 25 years ago, I have realized one thing: people have the wrong impression of war…they think war consumes everything in your day-to-day, but as my cousin mentioned to me last weekend… one of the greatest attributes of humans is that we adapt to whatever situation we are presented with.

And he is right; I remember that, in the middle of bombing, people would still have weddings, baptize their kids and go finding food. The parallel here is great. People assume that the Iran-US/Israel war is all people worry about in the Middle East right now, but no, people are planning ahead and companies as well.

Last month the company answered. Records on every single line of the income statement, a revenue target set when the company was founded was reached ahead of the plan, and the first dividend in its history. The stock gapped to an all-time high when it announced its Q2 results.

In this article, I raise my target by 13%, so there is still 34% upside on this opportunity.

Table of Contents

  • How the stock ranks

  • Q2 2026: the quarter the thesis stopped being a projection

  • Guidance: the floor moved up

  • Thesis scorecard after Q2 2026

  • Valuation: from $41.50 to $47

  • Risk register after Q2

  • Performance vs. peers

  • Verdict

TLDR

  • Q2 2026 was record-breaking on every line: revenue grew +59.1% y/y and beat consensus by 16%; adjusted EPS beat by 25%.

  • The $2B revenue run rate target arrived two quarters early. Management now calls $2B the FY2026 minimum, which is +52% growth.

  • Capital returns went from watch item to fact: a $0.10 quarterly dividend starts Q4 2026 and a $50M buyback is live.

  • Thesis scorecard: three pillars confirmed, two evolving. The DCF target moves from $41.50 to $47.

  • After +72% in five months, the risk/reward still clears 1 to 1.6. NESR stays a BUY with the target raised to $47.

How NESR ranks

RankedStocks.com scores NESR at 79, down from the 90 it carried when I published the deep dive.

Growth 95. Forward revenue growth scores in the top decile, and the 3-5 year EPS growth outlook scores higher still. This is the Jafurah and Kuwait ramp showing up in sell-side models.

Sentiment 99. The stock has beaten the sector on every trailing window, and analysts have nothing but Buys and Strong Buys on it.

Valuation 16. Every trailing multiple scores poorly after a +261% year. The forward multiples score better (you are paying today for earnings that arrive in 2027).

Profitability 43. Margins run under the high-margin names in the group because a MENA contract book trades peak pricing for volume durability, while its capital-efficiency metrics sit near the top of the same group. Same business quality argument as the deep dive: the model wins on utilization, overhead and multi-year contracts rather than on price.

Q2 2026: the quarter the thesis stopped being a projection

Revenue grew +59.1% y/y and +28.7% sequentially, beating consensus by 16%. Four Jafurah frac fleets ran through the whole quarter, conventional Saudi work was strong, and Oman and Egypt grew. Iraq, still under force majeure conditions from the conflict, was the one drag.

Adjusted EPS beat by 25% and adjusted net income grew +125.9% y/y. This is the operating leverage argument from the deep dive: incremental revenue on already-deployed fleets carries much higher incremental margin than the blended book.

Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 20.4%, a record $106.2M, with the war inside the number. The quarter absorbed $4M (80bps) of airfreight and contingency logistics to keep operations running through the conflict, plus a $1M credit loss provision. Stripping nothing out, the margin still expanded 140 bps sequentially. The 23-25% ambition for 2027-2028 remains the objective, and I think that Q2 was the first quarter that made the path to it much more visible.

Cash flow was the headline inside the headline. Operating cash flow of $174M and FCF of $99.9M in a single quarter, against $120.8M of FCF for ALL of 2025. Management flagged, unprompted, that $40M of that was quarter-end payables timing that reversed in early July, so the honest run-rate number is closer to $60M.

DSO hit a record low for a non-year-end quarter; the receivables build that used to feed the bear case is running in reverse.

The balance sheet crossed a line. Net debt fell to $99.6M, 0.3x annualized adjusted EBITDA (0.42x normalizing the payables timing), against a 1x target. Trailing ROCE reached 13.5%, up from 10.2% at year-end. The CFO called a zero net debt position within two years a realistic possibility.

Remember, this is the company that carried 5x leverage in 2021.

Guidance: the floor moved up

Two notes on reading this table. The capex raise from $165M to $210M-$215M is demand-driven: the fifth Jafurah fleet, recently awarded contracts in Kuwait, the UAE, and North Africa, and counter-cyclical equipment purchases. As a share of the higher revenue, it is still 10.5%, so the FCF conversion guide survived the raise. A higher capex guide in this sector is good news in my books: fleets are bought against multi-year contracts already awarded, so every extra dollar of capex maps to booked future revenue rather than to speculative capacity. The tax rate creep to 24% is mix, more profit coming from higher-tax jurisdictions, and it quietly costs about a point of net margin.

On credibility: management guided a $2B exit run rate for 2026 and delivered the run rate in Q2. They guided margins flat through a war and delivered 20.4% with conflict freight inside it. The one slip is timing on Kuwait tender awards, pushed a quarter, and the explanation (clients avoiding big awards to newcomers mid-conflict) cuts in NESR’s favour as an incumbent.

Share Beating The Tide: Stock Picks That Outperform

Thesis scorecard after Q2 2026

Pillar #1. Jafurah, from contract to cash: Confirmed and strengthening

Original thesis: the largest frac contract in oilfield services history converts into multi-year revenue with rising incremental returns as fleets deploy on capital already spent.

What happened since the deep dive: four fleets ran the full quarter, the fifth is shipped and waiting on Aramco’s deployment call, and Saudi drove most of a +28.7% sequential revenue move. Management now talks about beating Permian stage-count benchmarks.

Assessment: stronger than the deep dive assumed. The ramp arrived faster and the efficiency phase (the margin part of the story) is still ahead.

Pillar #2. Kuwait as the second engine: Evolving

Original thesis: Kuwait becomes NESR’s second-largest country on the back of a $3B+ tender wave, with awards through 2026 on 5-7 year contracts.

What happened since the deep dive: awards slipped about a quarter, to Q3-Q4 2026, with pricing already submitted. Meanwhile, NESR signed the Ahmadi Innovation Valley master technology agreement as one of four inaugural partners, a framework where a proven technology converts into multi-year revenue without a new tender, and won cementing awards worth $300M mid-conflict.

Assessment: directionally intact, one quarter later. The AIV agreement was not in my March thesis.

Pillar #3. The war-proof moat: Confirmed

Original thesis: a fully local workforce and in-country infrastructure make NESR harder to replace in a crisis rather than easier.

What happened since the deep dive: zero evacuations, zero contract interruptions, a 30-60-90 supply chain program that airfreighted critical materials at NESR’s own cost, and work captured from competitors who pulled staff. Larger rivals told the market the conflict hurt their MENA operations; NESR grew revenue +59% through the same months.

Assessment: the war did in one quarter what I expected to take years of tenders to prove. This pillar is now the company’s sales pitch, in the CEO’s own words, to every NOC in the region.

Pillar #4. FCF inflection and the balance sheet: Confirmed

Original thesis: front-loaded capex converts to cash as contracts scale; leverage falls below management’s 1x target and capital returns follow around mid-2026.

What happened since the deep dive: H1 FCF of $94.7M already covers 78% of 2025’s full-year figure. Net leverage 0.3x. And the capital return framework I listed as a catalyst became concrete: $0.10 quarterly dividend from Q4 2026 (a 1.2% yield at $34) and a $50M buyback with renewal evaluation in Q1 2027.

Assessment: delivered ahead of the timeline I wrote down.

Pillar #5. An underpriced compounder: Evolving

Original thesis: at $21 the market was pricing a 16% probability of my base case, per the Monte Carlo.

What happened since the deep dive: Mr. Market closed the gap. The stock is +72% since March against a target that moves +13%. In March, the setup was a $21.10 price against a $41.50 target and an $11 bear case, risk/reward of 1 to 2. Today it is $34.72 against $47 and a $27 bear, 1 to 1.6.

Assessment: the mispricing WAS the pillar, and much of it resolved in my favour. The gap that remains still clears my bar at 1 to 1.6.

Valuation: from $41.50 to $47

The updated DCF values NESR at $47 per share. Two assumptions did nearly all the work, and one worked against them.

You can view the DCF model here.

First, 2026 revenue growth goes from 35% to 52%. This is management’s own floor: H1 revenue of $925M is up +47% y/y, the $2B annual figure is now guided as a minimum, and Q4 is guided as the seasonal peak. The model lands at $2.01B. Everything after 2026 compounds off that bigger base; the years 1-5 average stays at 11.3% and does NOT assume the 3B3 stretch target ($3B run rate within three years), Kuwait mega-awards, ROYA or Syria. If those arrive, they are upside to $47, the same way Jafurah’s acceleration was upside to March’s $41.50.

Second, gross margin moves from 14% to 15% for 2026-2027. Q2 printed a record 15.6% gross margin with war logistics inside it, and the second half is seasonally stronger with Jafurah at cruise control. I hold the long-term margin path unchanged, still below management’s 23-25% EBITDA ambition throughout.

Working against them, the tax rate rises from 22.5% to 24%, matching guidance and the 24.5% H1 actual. I also now model the dividend ($0.10 in 2026 stepping to $0.40 in 2027).

I always like to do the exercise of getting to the market price by playing with the DCF assumptions. To make $34.72 the fair value, I have to keep 2026 exactly as guided (it is effectively banked) and then flatten everything after it: post-2026 growth cut in half and margins parked near 2025 levels forever. In other words, Mr. Market is paying full price for the year in hand and half credit for the Kuwait awards and the Jafurah efficiency phase.

The bear case also moved. March’s $11 assumed the war chokes the 2026 ramp; that window has closed, H1 is in the books. The new bear: Hormuz disruption drags into 2027, Kuwait awards go to the incumbents, 2027 revenue grows only +7% and margins stall near 20%. That is $430M of 2027 EBITDA at 6.5x forward EV/EBITDA, with near-zero net debt: $27 per share, 22% below today. Against $12.50 of upside to the $47 target, the setup is a risk/reward of 1 to 1.6. The floor sits far above March’s because H1 is banked, the dividend starts in Q4 and leverage is 0.3x.

If you know someone who owns the oil majors but has never looked at the picks and shovels underneath them, share this with them.

Share

Risk register after Q2

First, the war. Unchanged and still the most relevant one. Iraq remains under force majeure, Qatar LNG is still constrained, and the freight bill runs $4M a quarter. The post-conflict restart is a genuine catalyst (warm-stacked rigs across the Gulf need intervention work the day Hormuz reopens), but a longer war defers the 2027 tender cadence that my years 1-5 growth depends on.

Second, customer concentration is now rising. Aramco was 49% of revenue in 2025 and Jafurah’s ramp pushes that share up before Kuwait pulls it back down. The counterparty is the most profitable company on earth, so the risk is more on the pace of payments rather than on the payment itself.

Third, margin competition on uncommitted scope. The committed Jafurah work is locked; the uncommitted portion prices competitively, and the CEO has admitted tender pricing in the region is getting more competitive. If margins stall near 20%, the 23-25% ambition becomes less achievable, and my $47 loses its margin leg.

Fourth, the price is new. The stock has to digest +274% in twelve months; at 8.6x forward EV/EBITDA, delivery is now the expectation, and the second half needs $1.08B of revenue just to reach the floor.

The accounting-credibility risk from the deep dive comes OFF the register. All four material weaknesses were remediated by end-2025, six consecutive clean prints followed, and the company just upgraded its auditor from Grant Thornton Dubai to PwC for the 2027 audit after a competitive tender, with no disagreements on the way out. That was the discount that made $21 possible, and it is fading exactly the way the thesis said it would.

Performance vs. peers

NESR returned +274% over the past twelve months vs. a +28% median for the sector. The move came in three legs, each attached to a delivery event (the Jafurah ramp, the war resilience, Q2 earnings).

While oil prices have been volatile since I added the NESR position, they are at the same level as 5 months ago, but NESR’s stock price is up +72%. That tells me the market has found the story.

Verdict

I am raising the target from $41.50 to $47. NESR stays a BUY. The position stays in the portfolio untouched. The thesis is executing better than I wrote it; the dividend starts in Q4, and the Kuwait award list lands within two quarters. At $34.72, the stock offers $12.50 of upside to the target against $8 of downside to the $27 bear, a risk/reward of 1 to 1.6 with every catalyst on the list still ahead.
